route: Native TypeScript and plain CSS, served locally at /; translated-label demo at /?lang=de

requirementCoverage.evidence: artifact/invitation-copy.ts reusable factory, main.ts exact invitation URL, checked-in ES modules and styles.css; no framework, UI library or icons.
pending flag and aria-disabled/busy; evidence/browser-checks.json keyboard-and-pending confirms one write despite repeated submissions.
2000ms success reset timer; real-clipboard-and-timer confirms exact clipboard content and restored original label.
rejection-and-retry and unavailable-clipboard checks; inline explanation, selectable manual URL and keyboard retry.
Native button supports Tab/Enter/Space; polite atomic live status; 3px focus outline; measured translated button 242 by 70.78 CSS pixels.
Corrected 320 by 640 viewport test: exact German label wraps, button scrollWidth equals clientWidth, no document horizontal overflow; evidence/german-320-focus.png.
Small restrained example; artifact/README.md gives dependency-free Node24 startup and reuse/rebuild instructions; serve.mjs ran during browser checks.

assumptions: Requirement IDs were mapped in task order because the input lists IDs without per-ID descriptions.
The example is a single invitation control with a small contextual card; the ?lang=de route demonstrates only the requested translated button label.
Clipboard access requires localhost or HTTPS plus browser permission. The manual-copy field provides a fallback.
decisions: Used a native button with a pending guard and aria-disabled to preserve keyboard focus while ignoring duplicate clicks.
Kept progress, success and error announcements in one polite atomic live region.
Made the long label wrap naturally and used a 48px minimum target height.
Exported a factory with per-instance state, unique status IDs, and a destroy method that clears timers and avoids late DOM updates.
Supplied compiled JavaScript so the demo runs without installing dependencies.

checks.evidence: evidence/typescript.json: zero diagnostics, emitSkipped=false; compiled using installed TypeScript API.
Real Chrome clipboard matched URL; success visible after 1.1s; original label returned within 3.1s.
Tab + Enter triggered one request; repeated clicks ignored while pending; aria-disabled/aria-busy set and focus preserved.
Rejected clipboard showed inline permission guidance and manual URL; keyboard Space retry succeeded.
Unavailable API produced inline browser guidance and manual-copy field; retry button remained enabled.
Viewed evidence/german-320-focus.png, success.png and error.png: readable wrapped label, visible focus ring, restrained single-card treatment and inline error/manual-copy field.

Initial verifier exited before application checks with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME because of Windows ESM import syntax. Corrected to file:/// import; evidence/initial-run-error.txt retains the failure.

First successful run did not set the intended 320px viewport. Original results retained in evidence/browser-checks-initial.json. Corrected page.setViewportSize and reran all checks; see evidence/viewport-check-correction.txt.
Live status semantics and changing text checked in Chrome DOM; no screen-reader session executed.
Only installed Google Chrome was run; Firefox, Safari and physical touch devices were not available in this trial.

limitations: Screen-reader announcement behavior was not tested with assistive software; semantics were inspected.
Browser verification was limited to installed Chrome.
The translated demonstration changes the button label; all status and error copy remains English.
Two verification-tool errors were corrected and retained; final application browser checks all passed.
measurementAvailability: Exact token usage and monetary cost were unavailable to the worker.
